questions.question: Why doesn't updating an `Animated.Value` trigger a React re-render on every animation frame?
options: It does trigger a re-render every frame, that's expected
Animated.Value is intentionally kept outside React state, since re-rendering the component tree 60 times a second would be far too slow
Animated.Value can only be used outside of components
React Native disables re-renders while any animation is active
questions.explanation: Animated values live outside the normal React render cycle specifically so the animation can run smoothly without the overhead of a full component re-render on every frame.

questions.question: What does `useNativeDriver: true` actually change about how an animation runs?
options: It makes the animation duration shorter
It hands the whole animation to the native UI thread upfront, so it runs independently of the JS thread instead of requiring a bridge round-trip every frame
It disables the animation on Android only
It has no real effect, it's just a deprecated flag
questions.explanation: Without it, each frame requires sending the next value across the bridge from JS to native; with it, the native side drives the entire animation on its own.

questions.question: Why can't the native driver animate a property like `width` or `flex`?
options: Those properties don't exist in React Native
Changing them requires re-running JS-side layout logic, which only the JS thread can do — the native driver only handles properties like opacity/transform that don't affect layout
It's an arbitrary restriction with no technical reason
Native driver animations are always layout-safe
questions.explanation: Layout-affecting properties require recalculating the layout tree, which is JS-side work; the native driver is limited to properties (opacity, transform) that can be applied directly without touching layout.

questions.question: What is the key idea behind Reanimated's 'worklets' that makes gesture-driven animations smoother than the base Animated API?
options: Worklets run on a separate JS thread with higher priority
Worklets are small functions compiled to run directly on the UI thread, so a gesture can update the animation every frame with zero bridge round-trips
Worklets precompute every possible animation frame ahead of time
Worklets disable the JS thread entirely while active
questions.explanation: Because the worklet itself executes on the UI thread, gesture updates can drive the animation in real time without ever needing to communicate back to the JS thread mid-gesture.
